Items.Authors: Chris AS Parmenter, Nick R. Waltham, Matthew J. Clapp, Téa Seitis, Matthew Tildesley, Matthew Beasley, Todd J. Veach, Craig DeForest
Items.Title: Development and planned evolution of CCD camera electronics for the PUNCH Wide Field and Narrow Field Imagers
Items.Abstract: The Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) mission is a constellation of four satellites imaging the Sun in visible light from a Sun-synchronous low Earth orbit. It aims to improve our understanding of how the solar wind transitions from the Sun’s corona to the heliosphere.    We present the development and characterisation of the CCD camera electronics common to the Wide Field Imager (WFI) and Narrow Field Imager (NFI) instruments onboard PUNCH, which include RAL’s custom Correlated Double Sampling (CDS) Analogue-to-Digital Converter (ADC) and Digital-to-Analogue Converter (DAC) ASICs. In addition, future technology developments to further increase the performance and reliability of the PUNCH camera electronics are summarised.

Items.Authors: Jing Guo, Yongtian Zhu, Jiangpei Dou, Xi Zhang, Zhen Wu, Mingming Xu, Gang Zhao, Gang Wang, Bo Chen, Huatao Zhang, Zhonghua Lv
Items.Title: Development and testing of a ground-based high-contrast imager for exoplanet imaging
Items.Abstract: A ground-based high-contrast imager dedicated for exoplanet studies recently developed by Nanjing Institute of Astronomical Optics & Technology, CAS (NIAOT) under the supported from National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) is introduced. The instrument is designed to deliver an imaging contrast better than 10^(-5) in the near-infrared wavelengths, and its limiting magnitude is mv=13. Furthermore, the instrument is optimized to be used on 4-meter class telescopes and has a compact size of 920(L)×950(W)×370(H) mm^3. In this presentation, instrument performance in testing and calibration will be presented.

Items.Authors: Takahiro Nagayama, Hidehiko Nakaya
Items.Title: Development of 640×512 Pixel InGaAs Image Sensors for H and Ks Band Astronomical Observations
Items.Abstract: We are developing InGaAs image sensors for astronomical observations in  collaboration with Hamamatsu Photonics, Inc. (Japan). The sensors under  development features a pixel pitch of 20 μm and a total format of 640×512  pixels. The readout integrated circuit (ROIC) is a custom device newly  designed and optimized specifically for astronomical applications, and it  has already been completed and delivered.  Two types of InGaAs photodiode array are being prepared: one provides  sensitivity up to 2.1 μm at room temperature and is suitable for H band  observations, while the other offers sensitivity up to 2.6 μm at room  temperature for Ks band observations. In addition, a matured InGaAs photodiode  array with a 1.7 μm cutoff is being prepared for the J band. The hybridizations  of image sensors are scheduled to be completed in March 2026.  In this presentation, we will report on the fundamental performance  characteristics of these sensors.

Items.Authors: Chenhao Zhao, Yasuhiro Hirahara, Yuan Li, Biao Zhao, Shohei Negishi, Ryoichi Koga, Umi Enokidani, Hideo Matsuhara, Shunsuke Baba, Takao Nakagawa, Takehiko Wada
Items.Title: Development of a cryogenic high precision refractive index measurement system for CdZnTe using the minimum deviation method
Items.Abstract: We have developed a compact cryogenic system for high precision refractive index measurements of CdZnTe, aimed at supporting the optical design of the GREX PLUS high resolution spectrograph. The system is based on the minimum deviation method and incorporates improved vacuum rotation mechanics, non contact magnetic torque transfer, a low temperature ceramic thrust bearing, and flexible high purity copper thermal links. Together with narrow band mid infrared illumination and liquid nitrogen cooled InSb/MCT detectors using lock in detection, the setup enables stable angle measurements in the 4–20 K temperature range. The achieved accuracy of ∣δn∣<10^(-3) in the 10–18 µm wavelength region meets the requirements for designing high dispersion immersion gratings for space infrared instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Serena Farina, Leonardo Nassi, Paolo Nogara, Luca Schettini, Salvatore Incorvaia, Sergio D'Angelo, Mauro Fiorini, Marco Carminati, Giacomo Borghi, Carlo Fiorini, Michela Uslenghi
Items.Title: Development of a FUV photon counting detector prototype with a microchannel plate coupled to a low-noise custom readout ASIC
Items.Abstract: Microchannel-plate (MCP) detectors remain essential for far and extreme ultraviolet (FUV/EUV) astronomy thanks to their single-photon sensitivity and solar-blind response. In 2024, we developed a first prototype of an MCP readout based on a custom 32×32-pixel ASIC, integrating per-pixel charge shaping, event discrimination, and digital correction for charge sharing. This architecture achieves very low noise (~20 e⁻), enabling ALD MCPs to operate at low gain with high per-pixel count rates (up to 100 kcps). Building on these results, we are developing a second, improved version designed for larger detector formats, reduced power consumption, and enhanced robustness. The new system is currently under fabrication and will be tested in a dedicated UV vacuum chamber. This talk will summarize recent progress and outline future development paths.

Items.Authors: Tushar Ubarhande, Suvendu Rakshit
Items.Title: Development of aperture masking interferometry for 13.7m National Large Optical Telescope (NLOT), India
Items.Abstract: Aperture masking interferometry (AMI) enables high-angular-resolution measurements by directly sampling spatial frequencies in the Fourier plane, providing visibility amplitudes and closure phases. We present the development of an AMI system intended for the proposed 13.7 m National Large Optical Telescope (NLOT), India, capable of achieving a theoretical resolution of ≈10 mas at 650 nm. Our work includes a flexible simulation framework for any telescope aperture, laboratory validation using interchangeable aperture masks, and on-sky testing with a 30 cm telescope. Simulations generate u–v coverage, visibilities, PSFs, and realistic noise to optimize mask design and predict telescope performance. Laboratory interferograms match simulations and help identify issues such as alignment and bandwidth smearing. Initial on-sky results confirm the reliability of the mask and visibility pipeline, and we are preparing to deploy a prototype on the 1.3 m DFOT (Devasthal Fast Optical Telescope).

Items.Authors: Emma Floyd, Ian Schofield, Sam Rochelle, Ahshanul Haque, James J. D. Luis, Juan Altamirano, Chris Salcido, John Young, Siavash Norouzi
Items.Title: Development of automated alignment system control software for the Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer: towards maximizing science throughput
Items.Abstract: To maximize science throughput at the Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer (MROI), rapid and precise optical alignment is essential. This paper presents a scalable control interface designed to manage the facility's hardware, including motors, sources, and detectors. The architecture features an abstraction layer and a robust simulation mode that ensures system stability during hardware intermittency. Validated during MROI’s "First Fringes" on July 12, 2025, the system supports concurrent multi-user workflows to accelerate setup times. We discuss key lessons learned regarding the operator experience during on-sky commissioning and outline the roadmap for phased automation.

Items.Authors: Ettore Del Monte, Matias Antonelli, Marco Grassi, Filippo Mele, Riccardo Campana, Francesco Ceraudo, Giovanni Della Casa, Giuseppe Di Persio, Yuri Evangelista, Marco Feroci, Mauro Fiorini, Alessio Nuti, Giulio Orzan, Alexander Rachevski, Irina Rashevskaya, Gianluigi Zampa, Nicola Zampa, Giuseppe Bertuccio, Piero Malcovati, Giancarlo Pepponi, Francesco Ficorella, Michele Caselle
Items.Title: Development of multi-pixel silicon drift detectors for X-rays
Items.Abstract: The Pixelated silicon Drift Detector (PixDD) is a multi-pixel X-ray sensor based on the silicon drift technology on a 2D matrix of pixels with 300 micrometers pitch. The front-end ASIC, named RIGEL, has a 2D matrix of cells with sparse readout, fast response time, and good noise performance even at room temperature. Sensor and ASIC are interfaced using a die-level bump bonding technique. PixDD is an ideal focal plane sensor for X-ray concentrators and lobster-eye optics.  An improvement of PixDD is the Imaging drift edgeless array for X-rays (IdeaX), recently approved in the framework of the PRORIS program. In IdeaX we plan to develop an edgeless system based on a pixelated silicon drift detector and two ASICs (front-end and back-end) interconnected using through-silicon vias and bump bonding. This approach aims to minimise the dead area on the focal plane.   Here we present the measured performance of the existing 16 x 16 pixels prototype of PixDD and we discuss the IdeaX working plan.

Items.Authors: Haruaki Niinuma, Hiroshi Akitaya, Shuichi Gunji, Yoshifusa Ita, Kohji Tsumura, Hideo Matsuhara, Daisuke Yonetoku
Items.Title: Development of onboard image processing software for MONSTER on the HiZ-GUNDAM satellite
Items.Abstract: HiZ-GUNDAM is a future space mission designed to detect high-redshift gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) using both an X-ray telescope and a five-band visible/near-infrared telescope, MONSTER. Because the satellite’s real-time alert system cannot downlink raw images, image processing must be performed onboard. MONSTER detects roughly one thousand sources in the field of view, one of which is the GRB afterglow. Since transmitting information for all sources may be impossible, the system must identify only a few tens of afterglow candidates. To accomplish this, a lightweight decision-tree algorithm was developed that can run on the onboard computer. Using five-band photometric measurements, it narrows down the candidates to several tens. Using the constructed decision tree, when detector noise is ignored, the true afterglow at z > 6 is included among these selected candidates with nearly 100% probability. In this presentation, I describe the details of this onboard candidate-selection algorithm.

Items.Authors: Bastián Romero, Felipe Guzmán, Esteban Vera
Items.Title: Development of real-time piston sensing using a single-shot coded aperture instrument and deep phase retrieval
Items.Abstract: We address ELT co-phasing challenges with a single-shot complex field wavefront sensor. Using coded diffraction intensity images, we detect piston discontinuities from segments and spiders. We employ deep learning enhanced phase retrieval to ensure high fidelity, bypassing iterative computational bottlenecks. Experimental results demonstrate our neural network achieves the inference speeds necessary for real-time adaptive optics.

Items.Authors: Xiaofei Li, Shidong Shen, Xuhao Wu, Dehua Yang, Hua Bai, Yong Zhang, Xiangqun Cui
Items.Title: Development of Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensing for the 4-m segmented JUST telescope
Items.Abstract: The JUST telescope employs a primary mirror composed of two rings of hexagonal segments, forming a compound astronomical system with dual Nasmyth foci. This design brings challenges for wavefront reconstruction: a significant central obscuration caused by the secondary mirror and baffle, which reduces the effective aperture of the inner ring segments by up to 37%; and pupil rotation induced by the Nasmyth platform, introducing additional wavefront errors. To address the inner-ring obscuration issues, we developed a lenslet array switching mechanism for the Shack–Hartmann sensing, enabling adaptive sampling of the segmented wavefront. For pupil rotation compensation, a de-rotator assembly was integrated into the wide-field Nasmyth arm to stabilize the exit pupil. Numerical simulations verifies that this configuration achieve the resulting wavefront error with RMS value approximately 0.8 nm.

Items.Authors: Yanji Yang, Jia Ma, Jiehan Cao, Jia Wang, Jixin Feng, Juncheng Lu, Qian Zhang, Yusa Wang, Yong Chen, Bo Wang, Dianlong Wang, Langping Wang, Fei Ding, Jiadai Xue, Pengfei Qiang, Yongqing Yan, Lizhi Sheng, Yupeng Xu
Items.Title: Development of the focusing mirrors onboard eXTP
Items.Abstract: The eXTP mission has finished the phase B study. The eXTP satellites employs 9 X-ray focusing mirrors including 6 mirrors with the reflective layer of gold and 3 with that of nickel. By the end of 2025, we have finished four phototypes of the mirror module employing the nickel replica technoloty. During the testing of the phototypes manufactured by Media Lario and us, we found additional loss of the effective area by 10%. In this way, we have rechecked the margin of the design of the effective area, and added 5 inner most shells into the mirror module to increase about 40 cm2. Moreover, the thickness to radius ratio has also increased to 0.002 to manufacture the mirror shells with higher yield rates.

Items.Authors: Dervis Vernani
Items.Title: Development of the THESEUS IRT telescope refocusing system
Items.Abstract: THESEUS is currently one of three candidate missions for ESA's M7 call and is planned for a launch in 2037, following a final mission adoption in 2028. The THESEUS spacecraft includes a payload composed of three instruments, one of them being a 0.7 m class Korsch InfraRed Telescope (IRT). The thermo-optical stability of the IRT requires a tight control over the entire thermal operative range of the inter-mirror distance between the primary (M1) and secondary (M2) mirror. This inter-mirror distance is driven by the mechanical characteristics of the truss in which the M2 is integrated. The selected materials for the truss and its structural design quite likely cannot achieve the required optical stability, therefore a refocusing strategy needs to be developed allowing to accurately adjust the M1-M2 distance. In this paper we report about the development of a refocusing breadboard structures for the secondary mirror of the IRT telescope, including experimental characterization in vacuum.

Items.Authors: Charlotte Feldman, Alejandro Guzmán Cabrera, Roisin Ryan, Lauro Conti, Gillian I. Butcher, Anna Maskolenko, Paul R. Houghton, Daniel Schuppe, Vadim Burwitz
Items.Title: Development of the THESEUS SXI optics for ESA M7 candidate
Items.Abstract: The University of Leicester and the University of Tuebingen as joint PI institutes for the Soft X-ray Instrument (SXI) on THESEUS, an ESA M7 candidate mission, are responsible for the optic and detector development. The SXI consists of two identical Lobster eye modules with an 8x8 array of Micro Pore Optics (MPO), working in the energy range 0.3-5 keV. We present the progress of the development of the breadboard optic, including frame material trade off, X-ray results of MPOs and the breadboard itself and results from a thermal deformation study.

Items.Authors: Yuanpeng Gao
Items.Title: Digital twin modeling of large-aperture fast steering mirror for Space astronomical telescope
Items.Abstract: Driven by the critical demands of deep space exploration, modern space astronomical telescopes are evolving towards larger apertures and longer focal lengths. To ensure high-precision Line-of-Sight (LOS) pointing and image stability, large-aperture Fast Steering Mirrors (FSMs) are increasingly adopted in these optical systems. However, a critical challenge remains: how to accurately predict the FSM’s angular and mechanical states, efficiently tune closed-loop control parameters, and guarantee performance under on-orbit conditions characterized by limited monitoring capabilities and insufficient temporal resolution. To address these challenges, This paper proposes to establish a piezoelectric physics embedded neural network model, achieving high-fidelity modeling of large-aperture FSM over a wide frequency range. This study offers a scientific foundation for the status monitoring, maintenance, and performance evaluation of next-generation space mechanisms.

Items.Authors: François-Xavier Schmider, Olivier Lai, Hans-Peter Doerr, Max Görlach, Marcel Carbillet, Lyu Abe, Elora Lefebvre, Julien Dejonghe, Jean-Pierre Rivet, Markus Roth
Items.Title: Doppler imaging measurements in the visible with adaptive optics: improving and estimating the PSF for planetary atmosphere wind measurements
Items.Abstract: The AOC (Adaptive Optics at Calern) system is based on a 10x10 Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor and a 97-actuators deformable mirror, and installed on the 1-m C2PU telescope at Calern Observatory, near Nice. It aims at correcting turbulence for both stellar and planetary observations, in the visible (519nm) with the Doppler imager JOVIAL. Simulations of partial correction have been carried out to assess the performance of the system and the gain on accuracy in the velocity measurements.   We are developing performance evaluation tools for AOC, based on real-time telemetry. Additionally, we use a multi-frame blind deconvolution algorithm (MFBD) to estimate the point-spread function from a series of short exposures in the focal plane and compare it to the PSF retrieved from AO telemetry. We plan on using the reconstructed PSF to perform deconvolution on the Jupiter measurements to improve the wind profile determination.  We will present the methods, the observations and preliminary results

Items.Authors: Jade A. Pratt, Keith J. Nowicki
Items.Title: Dual-domain atmospheric turbulence compensation: design and prototype comparison with adaptive optics
Items.Abstract: Atmospheric turbulence limits ground-based image quality and is typically mitigated with adaptive optics (AO), which is costly and complex. This work presents a dual-domain turbulence compensation instrument on a Celestron C11 that splits the telescope beam into two arms sharing the same incoming wavefront. One arm is a conventional Shack–Hartmann AO system using a Thorlabs DMH40-P01 deformable mirror and WFS20-5C sensor in closed loop. The second arm records simultaneous image-plane and Fourier-plane data. A computational algorithm uses that joint image/Fourier sampling to infer and correct phase aberrations without hardware wavefront sensing. Simulations, laboratory tests, and early on-sky results will be used to compare results and operational complexity between AO and the dual-domain approach.

Items.Authors: Amir Ebadati Bazkiaei, Tayyaba Zafar, Nuria Lorente
Items.Title: DustRover: A Python Package for Modelling Dust Extinction Curves (Phase One)
Items.Abstract: We introduce DustRover, an open-source Python package designed to model dust extinction curves using multi-wavelength observations. DustRover supports optical/NIR spectroscopy, broadband photometry, and X-ray data within a unified framework, enabling robust analysis of spectral energy distributions. Its modular design separates data management, dust models, and MCMC-based statistical fitting, providing flexibility for both standard and custom extinction parametrisations. The package is highly user-oriented, using simple YAML configuration files and offering built-in visualisation tools for SEDs and extinction curves. We present the Phase One capabilities of DustRover, show applications to real GRB and QSO datasets, and outline planned advancements towards a fully automated dust-analysis pipeline.

Items.Authors: Juan Pablo Gil, Gaspar Fabrega, Pedro Silva, Nicolas Miranda
Items.Title: ELIANA: An Open Source Library for Observatory Log Analytics
Items.Abstract: ELIANA (Event Log and Incident Analysis) is an open-source Python library for log analytics, developed at the Paranal Observatory to support the analysis of instruments and telescopes. The library is built on top of pandas, allows dataset generation, ML modules, and parlogs-observations, a public dataset of logs for VLTI using the Auxiliary Telescopes distributed as Parquet files aggregated by instrument, time range, and subsystem. ELIANA provides machine learning modules including logistic-regression, Naive-Bayes, specialized tokenizers and NLP utilities. The library has been used to foster academic collaboration (graduate lectures, PhD work, internships) and is actively integrated in several operational tools at Paranal that combine logs with other data sources for troubleshooting and analysis. This contribution presents the architecture of ELIANA, describes the structure and intended use of the parlogs-observations dataset, and illustrates use cases for observatory operations.

Items.Authors: Alfred Miksch, Victoria Laidlaw, Olivier Fauvarque, Benoît Neichel, Ronny Ramlau
Items.Title: Enhanced nonlinear wavefront sensing for adaptive optics with a double iQuad sensor design
Items.Abstract: Advanced adaptive optics (AO) systems use Fourier-type wavefront sensing to correct optical distortions, and the iQuad wavefront sensor (WFS) is a recent addition to this category. Its four-quadrant phase mask can detect many wavefront features, but some components may be poorly seen, causing instability in the AO loop. A dual-path setup using two differently oriented iQuad sensors overcomes this limitation. To ensure accurate and stable iQuad wavefront sensing, a fast and efficient nonlinear Gauss–Newton algorithm is applied for wavefront estimation. Numerical simulations comparing single and double iQuad configurations show that the dual-sensor approach offers significantly improved performance.

Items.Authors: Sarah Kendrew, Michael Engesser, Kate Rowlands, Alberto Noriega-Crespo, Jonathan Aguilar, Stacey Alberts, Taylor Bell, Aarynn Carter, Misty Cracraft, Hannah Diamond-Lowe, Achrène Dyrek, Karl Gordon, Dean R. Hines, Bryan J. Holler, Kirsten Larson, David R. Law, Katherine Murray, Bryony Nickson, Andreea Petric, Michael Regan, Gregory C. Sloan, Beth Sargent, Sachindev Shenoy, Boris Trahin, Ian Wong
Items.Title: Enhancing the performance and capabilities of the MIRI instrument on JWST
Items.Abstract: MIRI, the Mid-Infrared Instrument on the James Webb Space Telescope, provides the only capability longward of 5 µm on the observatory. In this regime, it is providing order-of-magnitude improvements over past facilities in a wavelength range that is challenging or impossible to access from the ground. As such, MIRI occupies a unique parameter space and offers unparalleled capabilities in all areas of astrophysics. Several years into its operational lifetime, we continue to explore the full breadth of MIRI's potential and make operational improvements to MIRI to create new capabilities and enhance its scientific return. In this paper we will describe several such improvements, and their anticipated impact on MIRI and JWST science - focusing on improvements in detector noise performance, improved time-series capabilities,  enhanced efficiency and flexibility of coronagraphic imaging, and a wide-field slitless spectroscopy mode.

Items.Authors: Lionel Clermont, Céline Michel, Quentin Chouffart, Yuchen Zhao, Emmanuel Mazy, Ines Fuente, Federico La China, Bertrand Fougnie
Items.Title: Ensuring reliability in space: a closer look at the need for testing multiple optical payload units
Items.Abstract: Spaceborne optical payloads must undergo extensive testing before launch, verifying performance against expectations and generating input data for in-flight software. Recently, a trend has emerged to build multiple units of the same instrument. These can be launched together, increasing the total field of view coverage, or consecutively, extending mission's lifetime beyond that of a single payload and benefiting from economies of scale. This raises a crucial question: Should each model undergo ground testing, or is it sufficient to test just one and apply the findings to all? This presentation will address this question, discussing test and calibration results of 3 supposedly identical payload versions, comparing parameters such as MTF, distortion, polarization spectral properties, and stray light. Our findings indicate that while initial testing offers valuable insights, significant variations among the models necessitate thorough testing of each unit, at least for certain parameters

Items.Authors: Aditya R. Sengupta, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Emiel H. Por, Benjamin L. Gerard, Vincent Chambouleyron, Zoe M. Weber-Porter, Yoo Jung Kim, Stephanie E. Sallum, Kevin Bundy, Anna Gagnebin, Matthew DeMartino, Daren Dillon, Tara Crowe, Caleb Dobias, Stephen S. Eikenberry, Rodrigo Amezcua-Correa, Stephanos Yerolatsitis
Items.Title: Error budgeting and performance limits for joint imaging and wavefront sensing with a photonic lantern
Items.Abstract: The photonic lantern (PL) is a focal-plane wavefront sensor (WFS) that can be used for second-stage control of extreme adaptive optics (AO) systems. While the number of sensed modes and the dynamic range in each mode have been relatively well characterized, little attention has been paid to how photon noise and read noise impact the accuracy of PL wavefront reconstruction. Using simulations as well as experiments on the muirSEAL testbed, we compare the PL's sensitivity as a function of spatial frequency to that of existing WFSs, and present error budgets for representative second-stage observing configurations. We assess these metrics in the case where only a subset of PL ports are available for wavefront sensing and the remaining ports are used for science imaging. This work sets the stage for AO system design incorporating the PL as a joint WFS and imager, by determining observing configurations that optimally trade off between wavefront error and reconstructed image fidelity.

Items.Authors: Konrad R. Skup, Miroslaw Rataj, Piotr Wawer, Mateusz Sobiecki, Konrad Rutkowski, Przemysław Nita, Grzegorz Szymański, Marianna Fulara, Marcin Sobolewski, Nils Thernstrom, Łukasz Kuryłowicz, Daniel Połtorak, Aleksandra Mirońska, Marek Winkler, Maurycy Ciarka, Adam Sikorski, Roland Ottensamer, Gerald Mösenlechner, Marko Mecina, Armin Luntzer, Warren Holmes, Renaud Goullioud, Mauro Focardi, Eduardo Medinaceli , Raoul Grimoldi
Items.Title: ESA ARIEL FGS: instrument design and implementation
Items.Abstract: In this paper we present the Fine Guiding System (FGS), one of two scientific instruments on board ESA’s ARIEL mission, scheduled for launch in 2029. ARIEL will study hundreds of exoplanets to characterize their atmospheres, investigate chemical composition, cloud properties, and weather variability. FGS serves a dual purpose: it delivers dedicated scientific measurements through three photometric channels and a low-resolution near-infrared spectrometer, while also supporting the spacecraft with ultra-precise pointing. Following the instrument Critical Design Review (iCDR), the FGS has entered the phase of engineering qualification model integration and flight model preparation, marking a major step toward mission readiness.

Items.Authors: Ángela Hernández Delgado, Jorge Quintero Nehrkorn, Fernando Merlos-García, Josué Barrera Martín, Claudia Ruiz de Galarreta, Peter Dr Caligari, Manuel Collados Vera, Carmen Marillai Barreto Cabrera, Hector Socas-Navarro, Sergio Javier Gonzalez Manrique, Miguel Núñez Cagigal
Items.Title: EST Data Centre: challenges
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) is a 4.2-meter solar facility planned to operate seven instruments: three TIS/FBI systems, three IFS-M units, and the EMBER IFS-S. EST is expected to generate around 169 GiB/s and about 2.7 PiB of data per day, posing major challenges in both data rate and data volume. The data flow from the instruments will require high-performance connectivity at the telescope, while the projected ~80 PiB per year cannot be efficiently handled by a single monolithic data center due to cost, scalability, and reliability limitations. As a result, the EST Data Center (EST-DC) is conceived as a distributed European architecture that minimizes data movement and provides the necessary storage and computing resources, following the FAIR principles

Items.Authors: Pedro José García Martín, Miguel Núñez Cagigal
Items.Title: EST RAM analysis and consequent design and maintenance strategy
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) has passed successfully the Preliminary Design Review. The lifetime requirement of fifty years, together with other demanding requirements about its availability and reliability triggered a FMEA analysis mainly focused on developing robust maintenance strategies. We describe how RAM aspects drove some design choices as well as the selection and use of components. We report the preventive and predictive maintenance strategies, which we considered to minimize the risk of observation downtime in the high cost operational context of the EST.

Items.Authors: Maryam Raouph, Andreas Schrimpf
Items.Title: Evaluating natural magnitudes in the photometric system of astronomical plates
Items.Abstract: Accurate photometric calibration of historical astronomical plates is challenging due to mismatched spectral sensitivities with the passbands of modern calibration catalogs. We present a method to derive more accurate and consistent natural magnitudes for plate sources using Gaia DR3 BP/RP low-resolution spectra. By compiling spectral characteristic data for emulsion and filter combinations, and modifying for atmospheric reddening depending on air mass, we compute synthetic magnitudes, utilizing a catalog of Gaia spectral energy distributions (SEDs), via the GaiaXPy python library. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional color term corrections, revealing systematic errors up to ±0.3 mag. It also effectively corrects atmospheric effects at higher air masses (~0.2 mag). This method facilitates integration of historical plate data with modern observations, supporting precise time-domain studies across global photo plate collections.

Items.Authors: Diego Portero Rodríguez, Nicolás Adrián Rodríguez Linares, Hugo García Vázquez, José Javier Díaz García, Luis Fernando Rodríguez Ramos
Items.Title: Evaluating the application of an Integrated Photonics Wavefront Sensor (IP-WFS) using SAOS
Items.Abstract: Solar adaptive optics faces multiple challenges compared with night-time observations. One of these challenges is the low contrast between the Sun and the sky background. This requires the analysis of extended images instead of punctual sources, thereby limiting the spatial resolution in the wavefront sensing and increasing the complexity of the wavefront reconstruction. To overcome this boundary, this group proposed the application of a novel and interesting technology, called integrated photonics or photonics chips, to develop an integrated wavefront sensor, called "Integrated Photonic Wavefront Sensor (IP-WFS)". With the help of the new Solar Adaptive Optics Simulator (SAOS) developed for the EST, this work evaluates the features of the proposed wavefront sensor architecture, the accuracy of the wavefront reconstruction of extended objects for different levels of seeing, as well as technological questions, such as the efficiency of the light injection to single-mode waveguides.

Items.Authors: Durgesh Nandini Satpathy, Jonas Reiffers, Sebastian Albrecht, Thomas Bechteler, Andreas Lederhuber
Items.Title: Evaluation of power conditioning electronics for the satellite-borne X-ray wide field imager of the NewAthena project
Items.Abstract: NewAthena (New Advanced Telescope for High-Energy Astrophysics) is the L-Class flagship mission of the European Space Agency (ESA). NewAthena will be the largest satellite-based X-ray observatory and is planned to house two instruments: the X-IFU (X-ray Integral Field Unit) and the WFI (Wide Field Imager). The WFI instrument is developed by the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics (MPE) in collaboration with other partner institutes. One sub-system of the WFI is the Detector Electronics Subsystem (DES) which contains, inter alia, the Power Conditioning Module (PCM). The PCM is designed to generate high quality supply voltages for the WFI Camera Head (CH). This paper outlines the design, optimization, and evaluation of a representative subsection of commandable voltage source circuits on the PCM. Critical parameters, such as the stability of control circuits are determined. The function of the complete analogue control loop, including the switching mechanism, was verified.

Items.Authors: Manuel Gonzalez, Damien PRÊLE, Si Chen, Jean Mesquida, Bernard Courty, Alain Givaudan, Mael Le Cam
Items.Title: Evolution and demonstration of the warm front-end electronics for the X-IFU instrument on ATHENA
Items.Abstract: The Warm Front-End Electronics (WFEE) of the X-IFU instrument on ESA’s ATHENA mission provide TES and SQUID biasing, low-noise amplification, and multiplexing signal conditioning. We present recent advances following the development and successful testing of the WFEE Demonstration Model integrating the AwaXe_v3 ASICs in AMS 350 nm technology. A subsequent prototype generation in an ST node showed good performance but revealed reproducibility issues; this technology remains under investigation for future evolution. To ensure a robust path toward the Engineering Model (EM), a final AMS-based fabrication run has adopted a modular architecture with separate biasing and low-noise amplifier ASICs. We summarize the updated design, lessons learned, and initial results as the WFEE EM development progresses toward delivery in 2027.

Items.Authors: Matthew J. MacIntosh, Roberto Abuter, Federico Pellegrin
Items.Title: Evolving the methods of displaying real-time data from telescope control software
Items.Abstract: The European Southern Observatory’s (ESO) Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) real-time signal monitoring system has been modernized to replace a legacy architecture based on obsolete VME hardware and Tcl/Tk software. The new solution consolidates data acquisition, transport, and visualization on a single Linux workstation and introduces ESO’s Multicast User Datagram Protocol Interface (MUDPI) as the real-time data distribution layer. This enables seamless streaming of signals from the VLTI reflective memory network and also allows monitoring of real-time data from the deterministic network of ESO’s Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The user interface has been re-implemented in Python using the Qt framework, providing a flexible and responsive environment for signal selection and display.

Items.Authors: Wei Li
Items.Title: eXTP SFA-T camera status and design
Items.Abstract: The enhanced X-ray Timing and Polarimetry mission-eXTP is a scientific space mission designed to study the state of matter under extreme conditions of density, gravity and magnetism. One of the payloads is the Spectroscopic Focusing Array (SFA), an X-ray focusing telescope array. Each telescope setup consists of a mirror module, an electron deflector, a filter wheel, and a focal plane camera.   Five focal plane cameras are equipped with SDD, earning their telescopes the designation SFA-T (T for Timing), highlighting the SDDs' superior timing precision. Each of the SFA-T camera includes one filter wheel, one detector array, and one electronic box.

Items.Authors: Jingyi Zhang, Charlotte Guthery, Michael Bottom, Sébastien Vievard, Antonin Bouchez
Items.Title: Fast and furious on OSIRIS: improving AO performance with focal plane wavefront sensing at W. M. Keck Observatory
Items.Abstract: Quasi-static errors, such as non-common path aberrations and co-phasing errors, remain a key limitation to AO performance, and are now the largest part of the AO error budget at W. M. Keck observatory. Fast and Furious is a focal plane wavefront sensing/correction algorithm that runs concurrently with science observations, without requiring any extra hardware, diversity frames, or complex optical models. Now facilitized on NIRC2, it converges within ~5 minutes and consistently delivers Strehl ratio improvements of 10-15%.    We are now funded to expand this algorithm to all Keck AO instruments, and present our first expansion with OSIRIS, an integral field spectrograph and imager. The algorithm typically converges within 10 minutes, showing substantially improved PSF quality. We also present expansions to the functionality and scope of F&F on Keck including 1) its use with laser guide star mode,2) its use with field tracking mode, and 3) use with the new high-order deformable mirror.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo Cianniello, Vincenzo De Caprio, Christian Eredia, Enrico Cascone
Items.Title: Finite element analyses of the MORFEO Main Support Structure towards final design review
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. This paper offers an overview of the finite element analyses of the MORFEO Main Support Structure (MSS) for its structural validation at global level implementing the last mechanical updates. During 2023 MORFEO passed the Preliminary Design Review and now is approaching to Final design review. The models, developed by WP PMO in INAF - Observatory of Naples, are validated through FEM Analysis approach, utilizing CAD (Autodesk Inventor) and CAE (Ansys Workbench) software. In order to have a lighter model for the MORFEO MSS, and shorter computational times, simplified FE model than the whole 3D CAD have been developed. This paper is demonstrated that this method provides accurate results at global level.

Items.Authors: Edgar Ligon, Rainer Köhler, Karolina Kubiak, Douglas R. Gies, Narsireddy Anugu, Theo ten Brummelaar, Victor Castillo, Christopher Farrington, Becky Flores, Ludovic Grossard, Cyprien Lanthermann, Olli W. Majoinen, Heven D. Renteria, Francois Reynaud, Stephen Ridgway, Gail Schaefer, Nic Scott, Nils Turner, Norman L. Vargas, Craig Woods
Items.Title: First fringes of the CHARA Michelson Array Pathfinder Project
Items.Abstract: The Center for High Angular Resolution Astronomy (CHARA) Array currently consists of 6 telescopes at fixed positions, connected by vacuum pipes to the delay lines. The CHARA Michelson Array Pathfinder (CMAP) project includes two major components: 1) a mobile telescope that can be placed at a number of locations, and 2) a fiber optic relay system to transport light to the beam combining facility. We present our first on-sky fringes and the work done to reach this result.

Items.Authors: Charles Sallard, Patrice Martinez, Lyu Abe, Kian Milani
Items.Title: First laboratory demonstration of iEFC for high-contrast imaging at small angular separation on ELT scales
Items.Abstract: Implicit Electric Field Conjugation (iEFC) is a model-free wavefront control method that creates and maintains dark holes using real calibration data. We present the first demonstration of iEFC at very small angular separations, producing a 1–4 λ/D dark hole on a segmented pupil in H band using the SPEED testbed.  SPEED’s ELT-oriented design, including a reflective PIAACMC coronagraph and multi-plane DM architecture, enables compact dark holes at aggressive IWAs. These results demonstrate that combining iEFC with SPEED’s WFC architecture provides a valuable R&D pathway toward future ELT-class high-contrast instruments, ultimately aiming to reach contrasts on the order of 10⁻⁷.

Items.Authors: Anthony Meilland, Florentin Millour, Jeronimo Calderon Gomez, Stéphane Lagarde, Julien Dejonghe
Items.Title: First laboratory results from SPINER echelle interferometry and prospects for future instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Spectro-interferometry enables detailed studies of astrophysical objects by probing their geometry as well as their physical, chemical, and dynamical properties across different wavelengths, but current instruments are limited in either spectral resolution or bandwidth. To overcome these limitations, we introduced SPINER in 2024, a concept based on Echelle dispersion for spectro-interferometry, and developed the first visible multi-order test bench covering 600–900 nm at a high spectral resolution of R=20,000. Here, we present our first in-lab results, characterize the prototype’s performance, and discuss prospects for implementing SPINER in the visible and near-infrared on facilities such as the VLTI and CHARA arrays, opening new opportunities for high-resolution studies of stars, disks, and exoplanetary systems.

Items.Authors: Sébastien B. Vievard, Elsa Huby, Sylvestre Lacour, Olivier Guyon, Manon Lallement, Mathias Nowak, Yoo Jung Kim, Aidan Walk, Jehanne Sarrazin, Sergio Leon-Saval, Christopher Betters, Julien Lozi, Miles Lucas, Vincent Deo, Michael Fitzgerald, Barnaby Norris, Thayne Currie, Guy Perrin
Items.Title: FIRST-PL: commissioning the first visible photonic lantern spectrograph for sub-diffraction-limit astronomy on Subaru/SCExAO
Items.Abstract: FIRST-PL (Fibered Imager foR a Single Telescope - Photonic Lantern) is a newly commissioned visible-light instrument on Subaru/SCExAO achieving spectroscopy below the diffraction limit. The instrument uses a Photonic Lantern—converting multimode fiber into 19 single-mode outputs—feeding a mid-resolution spectrograph (R~3000, 630-790 nm). On-sky performance demonstrates 40% injection efficiency at 680 nm (Strehl ~30%) and 12× throughput improvement over single-mode fibers. Three operational modes enable spectro-astrometry (50 microarcsecond precision demonstrated on β-CMi), image reconstruction, and high-contrast imaging (contrast ~1000 at 100 mas). Science applications include mapping evolved star environments, resolving close binaries, and detecting Hα emission from accreting protoplanets. FIRST-PL represents a significant advancement in high-throughput photonic instrumentation for ultra-high-resolution astronomical imaging.

Items.Authors: Anna Tosolini, Milo Buitrago-Casas, Savannah Perez-Piel, Juan Carlos Martinez-Oliveros, Anton Tremsin
Items.Title: Flight results and calibration of the Timepix3 detector onboard the FOXSI-5 sounding rocket
Items.Abstract: The Focusing Optics X-ray Solar Imager (FOXSI-5) sounding rocket will refly in May, 2026; we will highlight flight results of the Timepix3 detector from launch at Poker Flat Research Range in Alaska. In preparation for launch, we present the new calibration procedure of the Timepix3 detector onboard the rocket payload, as well as subsequent detector testing during rocket integration at White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. The Space Sciences Laboratory (SSL) is the first to apply the Timepix3 detector to a sounding rocket mission, and accurate calibration of the detector ensures that data can be reliably converted into photon energy, count rate, and timing. The calibration procedure was fully conducted at SSL, utilizing an environmental chamber for thermal testing, 241Am and 133Ba sealed sources, and four metallic foils fluoresced by a Mini-X2 X-ray generator.

Items.Authors: Iremsu Taskin, Olivier Absil, Jalo Nousiainen, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Markus Kasper
Items.Title: Focal-plane wavefront control using reinforcement learning for high-contrast imaging
Items.Abstract: High Contrast Imaging (HCI) on ground-based telescopes suffers from phase aberrations on the observed wavefront caused by atmospheric turbulence. Adaptive Optics (AO) systems are adept at correcting these aberrations, but fall short in the correction of non-common path aberrations (NCPAs). NCPAs arise because the wavefront sensor (WFS) measures and corrects a wavefront that is different from that affecting the science images, thus requiring additional intervention. This work makes use of focal-plane wavefront sensing and reinforcement learning (RL) to address the wavefront aberrations caused by NCPAs. The PO4NCPA algorithm utilizes sequential phase diversity to address phase ambiguities, and is tested on a simulation designed for the Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) instrument. Follow-up laboratory testing is conducted in the GHOST bench with the ultimate goal of optimizing RL for on-sky testing.

Items.Authors: Kirill Makan, Anastasia Galkin, Simeon Reusch, Wail Abbas Ahmed
Items.Title: Focus on data publishers - Daiquiri framework for publishing astronomical data
Items.Abstract: At the Leibniz Institute for Astrophysics Potsdam (AIP), we use the Daiquiri framework and the containerized environment dq-dev to host, curate, and publish terabytes of astrophysical data. Dedicated web applications allow scientists from around the world to run SQL queries and retrieve their desired data in a reasonable amount of time. Key features of Daiquiri include access to SQL databases, the ability to upload VOTables, VO TAP, and Datalink protocol access, and the ability to download data in various formats, such as VOTable, FITS, and Parquet. Daiquiri supports sophisticated user management and data access rights. All components are open-source software available on GitHub: https://github.com/django-daiquiri/.    This contribution will focus on Daiquiri features that support data publishers' tasks once the data is in the database.

Items.Authors: Amna Waris, Chris Waring, Bradley Frank, Noah Schwartz, Charlotte Bond, Maxime Dumont, Douglas Harvey, Ilgin Okan, Maia Jones
Items.Title: FPGA accelerated machine learning for adaptive optics: a hardware-in-the-loop prototype
Items.Abstract: This work presents a hardware-in-the-loop prototype built on the AMD Versal Vision platform that pairs live sensor input with on device machine learning inference to investigate compact, embedded approaches to AO processing. The prototype builds on two earlier hardware demonstrators: a real-time imaging pipeline on an AMD Kintex UltraScale, and a machine-learning regression model for mirror alignment that achieved wavefront errors of around 6 nm RMS when deployed on a Versal AI Core. By integrating these strands, the system provides a platform for testing embedded ML pipelines under AO-relevant timing conditions and exploring their potential use in future low-power AO architectures.

Items.Authors: Joshua Liberman, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Jared R. Males, Aditya Khandelwal, Stephanie Rinaldi, Jay Kueny, Katie Twitchell, Joseph D. Long, Ewan S. Douglas, Lauren Schatz, Jennifer Lumbres
Items.Title: Freezing the speckles: focal plane wavefront sensing with the Spatially Clipped Self-Coherent Camera
Items.Abstract: The Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs) and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) require active speckle suppression to directly image exo-Earths. Focal plane wavefront sensing and control (WFSC) allows us to detect and remove time-varying speckles. The self-coherent camera (SCC) modifies a standard coronagraph design, creating a reference electric field that interferes with speckles in the final focal plane to form Fizeau fringes. However, the classic SCC needs oversized optics, limiting its implementation. We propose a new variant, the Spatially-Clipped Self-Coherent Camera (SCSCC). Our SCSCC reduces overall beam footprint and boosts sensor resolution by 3x. We present the SCSCC optical design combined with the photon-resolving Hamamatsu camera. We demonstrate high speed WFSC and active dark hole maintenance with the SCSCC in the lab, exploring the sensor’s robustness to time-varying speckles. The SCSCC is a valuable wavefront sensor for the upcoming HWO mission and the next-gen ELTs.

Items.Authors: Alan W. McConnachie, David Del Rizzo, Alexis Hill, Scott Roberts
Items.Title: From blue-skies to the night sky: enabling strategic R&D in the era of world observatories
Items.Abstract: With the construction of the Square Kilometer Array (SKA) at radio wavelengths, the Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs) at OIR wavelengths, and the ongoing scientific exploitation of the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) at mm/submm wavelengths, it is clear that astronomy is in the era of world observatories. None of these observatories or instruments would exist – and none of their future instruments will exist – without investment in strategic R&D by observatories and other groups to enable the next generation of instruments. I present case studies from the NRC Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Center – including radio correlators and receiver components, antenna design, and adaptive optics – to track the evolution of certain technologies from blue-sky concepts all the way to deployment on premier international facilities, where I try to identify commonalities, from how the idea was generated to key moments in the development pipeline.

Items.Authors: Christoph Tenzer, Paul Hedderman, Mariachiara Celato, Alejandro Guzman Cabrera, Shaymaa Hussein, Joerg Bayer, Gabriel Cobos Tello, Denis Tcherniak, Irfan Kuvvetli, Desiree Della Monica Ferreira, David Blanquez Sese
Items.Title: From detection to slew: autonomous payload operation in the THESEUS mission
Items.Abstract: THESEUS is an ESA M7 candidate mission designed to expand the discovery of high-energy transients across cosmic history, with a focus on GRBs as probes of the early Universe and multi-messenger sources. Its payload combines the wide-field imager instruments XGIS (2 keV - 10 MeV) and SXI (0.3 - 5 keV) with an IR telescope (IRT) for immediate slew, follow-up and redshift measurement. Three Instrument Data Handling Units (I-DHUs) provide power, control, and on-board processing for XGIS, SXI, and IRT, linked via SpaceWire for high-speed coordinated operations. Autonomous detection is enabled by the Master DHU Software Module (MDSM), which validates triggers, manages modes, issues alerts, and requests spacecraft slews. When XGIS or SXI detect a transient, the DHUs perform rapid validation and the MDSM initiates Burst/Slew Mode, updates the mission timeline, and broadcasts alerts via the Fast Burst Alert System to enable prompt IRT localisation and spectroscopy.

Items.Authors: Kangning Wang, Sizhe Wen, Jing Chen, Yanlei Wen, Zhiguo Jiang, Danpei Zhao, Haopeng Zhang
Items.Title: From Raw Telemetry to Calibrated Space-Object Catalogs: A Self-Calibrating Pipeline for a Space-Based Star-Field Imager
Items.Abstract: Space-based optical sensors are becoming an important component of space situational awareness (SSA), but their data processing chains are often fragmented across separate decoding, calibration, detection, and photometry tools, which complicates uniform deployments for on-orbit experiments and small demonstration payloads. We present an integrated, catalog-driven data reduction pipeline for space-based star-field imagery that produces astrometrically and photometrically calibrated space-object catalogs directly from downlinked telemetry. The pipeline outputs a structured space-object catalog containing pixel coordinates, sky coordinates, and brightness estimates, and is implemented as a modular software system suitable for both ground-based post-processing and future on-board deployment.

Items.Authors: Öykü Selimoğlu Galvan
Items.Title: From scientific ambition to operational reality: an integrated risk management methodology for end-to-end astronomical projects
Items.Abstract: This article proposes an Integrated Risk Management Methodology (IRMM) designed for systematic application across the entire lifecycle of all projects within the astronomy. The primary objective of the article is to present standardized guidelines for the continuous identification, assessment, and treatment of risks, thereby optimizing project outcomes and ensuring successful delivery from a risk management perspective.  Successful IRMM implementation necessitates a prerequisite cultural and systemic evolution within astronomy organizations, demanding enhanced accountability. Crucially, this evolution must integrate proactive technology obsolescence management, supply chain risk mitigation, and rigorous international interface control to mitigate the unique systemic vulnerabilities of custom, collaborative projects. This process culminates in the formal handover of residual risks and risk-based decisions to the final asset owners, the observatory operations team.

Items.Authors: Daniel S. Dahl, Nathan K. Long, Barnaby Norris, Christopher H. Betters, Akira Rodziewicz-Ryan, Jin Wei, Sergio Leon-Saval
Items.Title: From simulation to demonstration: hybrid mode-selective photonic lanterns for simultaneous optimal fibre injection and wavefront sensing
Items.Abstract: Photonic lanterns convert a multimode point-spread function at the telescope focal plane into multiple stable single-mode outputs that encode the incident wavefront, enabling sensitive focal-plane wavefront sensing. Hybrid mode-selective photonic lanterns (HMS-PLs) extend this concept by isolating the fundamental mode into a dedicated output while allowing the higher-order modes to be sensed separately and used to drive an adaptive-optics system for zero-NCPA, optimised single-mode injection.  We report the first fabrication and H-band laboratory characterisation of an HMS-PL and compare the results with Lightbeam simulations. The strong agreement between measurement and simulation demonstrates the viability of HMS-PLs as both efficient mode filters and powerful wavefront-diagnostic elements, supporting their use in future astronomical instruments such as Seidr within the ASGARD suite at the VLTI.

Items.Authors: Elisa Portaluri, Simone Di Filippo, Tânia Sofia Gomes Machado, Davide Greggio, Maria Bergomi, Roberto Ragazzoni, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Alessandro Ballone, Federico Battaini, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Demetrio Magrin, Valentina Viotto, Jacopo Farinato, Mauro Centrone, Gianluca Di Rico, Marco Faccini
Items.Title: From simulations to the telescope: performance assessment of the Ingot WFS
Items.Abstract: The Ingot WFS is a new class of sensor proposed to mitigate the significant geometric differences between Laser (LGSs) and Natural Guide Stars, a challenge amplified in the new generation of extremely large telescopes (ELTs). The I-WFS is designed for an optical system featuring a sufficiently large aperture and a laser launcher located outside the telescope pupil and is specifically conceived and optimized to accommodate the extended nature of LGSs. In this work, we discuss the current state-of-the-art of performance assessment through simulation runs, presenting promising results in terms of incorporating source geometry and reconstructing the atmospheric turbulence. We also outline the path toward our ultimate goal: performing an on-sky validation experiment on a facility configuration reproducing the main characteristics of an ELT. In parallel, we plan the assembly of a portable, standalone system, including the Ingot prism prototype, compatible with the facility interfaces.

Items.Authors: Emaad Paracha, Steven J. Benton, Aurelien A. Fraisse, Ajay S. Gill, John W. Hartley, Bradley Holder, William C. Jones, Lun Li, Richard J. Massey, Jacqueline E. McCleary, Johanna M. Nagy, C. Barth Netterfield, Susan F. Redmond, Jason D. Rhodes, L. Javier Romualdez, Jürgen Schmoll, Mohamed M. Shaaban, Sayan Saha, Bryce Warren, Jason Brown, Peter Bartosik, Ben Boyd, Pablo Trujillo, Philippe Voyer
Items.Title: From Sky to Screen - Improving File Downlinking over Error-Prone, Omni-directional Links from the Stratosphere
Items.Abstract: Long-duration stratospheric balloon missions must transmit large volumes of scientific and telemetry data over variable, omni-directional links prone to packet loss and bandwidth fluctuations. To address this, we developed a semi-autonomous file-downlink system for high-altitude astronomy missions such as SuperBIT and its successor, GigaBIT. The system comprises a payload client, ground server, and cleaner program capable of operating across UDP and TCP links. The client manages a dynamic queue of data and divides them into fixed-size chunks with metadata, enabling resumable transfers and selective retransmissions. This chunk-level approach ensures only corrupted data is resent, reducing bandwidth usage. The system helps increase overall throughput, substantially improving telemetry downlink in constrained stratospheric telescope missions. This talk presents the system design and protocol behaviour, along with the performance during SuperBIT’s final flight.
